messages:
amanda (Support): FYI escalation from @luis — Acme integration failing when using our tool call API. They send a tool arg that contains raw double quotes and we throw a 400. Customer says it used to work in their dev env.

luis (Customer): hey support — our job posts to /v1/call-tool with body: see below. We started seeing 400s last deploy. In our app we build the args string by hand.

luis (Customer): ```
POST /v1/call-tool HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "tool": "search_db",
  "args": "{ \"query\": \"title:\\"CEO\\" AND site:\\"acme.com\\"\" }"
}
```

amanda (Support): Thanks. Repro steps and raw error from our edge: ``HTTP 400 - invalid_request: tool args failed schema validation: invalid JSON in 'args' at position 18``. The parser fails because of nested unescaped quotes inside the args string. Customer is using literal escaped quotes incorrectly (double-escaping confusion).

dev_jay: ok, looks like two problems: 1) they send "args" as a stringified JSON that itself contains unescaped quotes (they tried escaping once for JS and again for our payload), 2) our error message is not actionable. Suggest we return a clearer message indicating the invalid escape sequence and show an example.

ingrid (SRE): can you paste the service log snippet? Also what's the SDK version? the recent string-encoding guard landed in 2026-01.

amanda (Support): logs: ```
2026-02-18T14:22:11Z request_id=abc123 level=error msg="args parsing failed" err="Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 24"
stack: json.parse -> validateToolArgs -> callToolHandler
```

dev_jay: thanks. Repro locally with curl: 

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-tool \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"tool":"search_db","args":"{ \"query\": \"title:\\"CEO\\" AND site:\\"acme.com\\"\" }"}'
```

dev_jay: If they intend args to be an object, the correct body should be: 

```json
{
  "tool": "search_db",
  "args": {
    "query": "title:\"CEO\" AND site:\"acme.com\""
  }
}
```

amanda (Support): customer says their integration is old and uses string concat. They can't migrate instantly. Is there a safe server-side fallback we can offer?

dev_jay: short answer: we should not silently accept invalid JSON. Long answer: we can provide a helpful 400 that includes a hint: e.g., "args expected an object or valid JSON string; found invalid escape sequence near '\"CEO\"'". Also provide workaround: pass args as base64 or escape inner quotes properly. Example workaround: 

```json
{
  "tool": "search_db",
  "args": "{\n     \"query\": \"title:\\\\"CEO\\\\" AND site:\\\\"acme.com\\\\\"\"\n  }"
}
```

ingrid (SRE): from ops: deploying a change that improves error message is fine. But do NOT implement tolerant parsing that tries to auto-correct — that can mask bugs and open security holes. :no_entry_sign:

amanda (Support): noted. Customer is asking for a short-term patch. They accepted two options: 1) SDK quick patch: helper that properly stringifies nested JSON before sending, 2) server returns a detailed hint and links to docs.

dev_jay: I'll draft a small SDK helper in node: `function safeArgs(objOrString){ return typeof objOrString==='string' ? JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(objOrString)) : objOrString }` — but careful: JSON.parse will throw if string invalid, so better to detect common patterns and give actionable error. I'll open a PR for the SDK.

amanda (Support): please also add a doc snippet we can paste to customers. Link to internal KB: https://docs.redwood.com/tool-calls#args and paste the snippet that shows correct vs incorrect.

amanda (Support): @deploy-bot any chance we can get the error-message patch into canary today? Customer is high-touch. :pray:

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to canary in 15 minutes (sha: d4f7a2). See pipeline: https://ci.redwood.ai/1245

dev_jay: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/sdk-node/pulls/487 — adds `validateToolArgs()` with better error details and test cases covering nested quotes, trailing commas, and common JS-escaped payloads.

amanda (Support): thanks — I'll reply to customer with the workaround + ETA on server patch. Also note: add example showing their original payload and the corrected version.

luis (Customer): thanks team — will try the patched SDK and report back. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup: 

amanda (Support): follow-up: after canary deploy, we saw a 90% reduction in these exact 400s from the Acme account. Filing internal postmortem to update onboarding docs and the quickstart.

amanda (Support): action items: [dev_jay] open SDK PR (done), [ingrid] ship canary (done), [amanda] send customer note + KB snippet (in progress).
